requirements.title: Electronic and movement-control effects

Warp disruption, capacitor drain, signature amplification and targeting interference stay deferred (FeatureSpec02 2).

requirements.title: Fresh campaign completes Scout with the starting fit
requirements.extent: Delivered: the original starting fit completes Pirate Scout, returns and reopens without offline progress.

requirements.title: Three hulls, 26 functional modules and the ammunition floor
requirements.extent: Three hulls, all 26 combat modules (the web completed in phase 4), the 16-charge ammunition floor with family and size coverage, schema, reference, localization, compatibility and availability checks; the v0.2-phase-4 content floor holds the complete catalog.

requirements.title: Buy, switch, fit inactive ships and transfer cargo
requirements.extent: Delivered in phase 1.

requirements.title: Six reference fits and same-hull preference reversals
requirements.extent: Phases 2-4: all six reference fits are authored and validated as legal and obtainable, two per hull with different weapon families, covering active shield, active armour, passive shield, a web-assisted turret fit and guided combat. Phase 6: the seeded fit-versus-site matrix flies every reference fit, fully supplied, at all twelve sites over ten fixed seeds with one command policy per fit and one target priority per site, and holds thirteen comparisons declared in advance with their metric. Each hull has a same-hull reversal: frigate autocannons beat guided launchers at Knife Fight and lose at Longshot Picket; blaster-and-web beats artillery at Armored Hold and loses at Longshot Picket; cruiser guided launchers beat railguns at Knife Fight and lose at Crossfire.

requirements.title: Turret, ammunition, defence, capacitor and size choices with traces
requirements.extent: Phases 2-3: projectile, hybrid and guided families in small and medium sizes; size enforcement before and at commit; registered passive operators for shield capacity and recharge, capacitor recharge, family damage, tracking and guided application, all through the common stacking pipeline with traces and offline behaviour. Phase 6 tuned the magnitudes against the fit matrix: small blaster damage 2.0 to 2.4, small artillery 2.6 to 2.4, small guided launcher cycle 6 s to 5 s.

requirements.title: Guided weapons formula and flight boundaries
requirements.extent: Phase 3: guided application formula, launch-to-impact projectiles, expiry, target loss, source destruction, simultaneous contact and expiry, mixed turret and launcher ammunition, NPC launchers and save/reopen in flight.

requirements.title: Player and NPC webs
requirements.extent: Lock, range and capacitor at start and completion; refresh at the expiry instant; multiplying sources and the floor; braking through the movement controller; source destruction, target destruction and departure; starvation, pause and mid-effect resume; the same rules for the opponent's web; projection, tactical tether, notification and loss-report explanation.

requirements.title: Ten NPC profiles across five archetypes
requirements.extent: Ten profiles, two per archetype, each held by content validation to its role and archetype-defining modules; small integration encounters show each archetype's observable behaviour through the shared opponent adapter. Phase 5 places every archetype profile in the twelve-site ladder, and the release floor requires it.

requirements.title: Twelve-site ladder in three bands
requirements.extent: Phase 5: twelve distinct templates, four in each of the entry, developed and advanced bands, each with a decision, recommendation and weakness disclosed before warp, archetype threats, and four fit-sensitive sites (Knife Fight, Armored Hold, Range Check, Screened Battery). Every site is selectable and reachable from a new campaign with no hidden gate or player scaling, and is completed repeatedly with the full bounty by a fit made for it; each fit-sensitive site punishes the fit its briefing names. The destination chooser groups and filters by band without removing entries.

requirements.title: Ten module drops and one-time reward materialisation
requirements.extent: Phase 5: the ladder's opponents can drop seventeen module definitions across weapons, defence, capacitor and weapon support, and propulsion and control, including small and medium launchers and a medium afterburner, with a starter-fittable drop in every band; every drop is also sold. Disclosure is derived from the same loot tables, with each opponent's chance and quantity, and states that loot is not guaranteed. One-time bounties, wreck materialisation, retreat and return, save and reopen, and player wrecks surviving a fresh attempt are covered. Phase 6: a career that leaves every module drop in the wrecks reaches the destroyer after 10-11 sorties and the cruiser after 26, on bounties, salvage and the market alone. A wreck that expires while a ship approaches it now stops that ship safely.

requirements.title: Career runs buy and use both hull upgrades
requirements.extent: Phase 6: careers from a new campaign buy and fly both hull upgrades through ordinary play - the destroyer package after 9 sorties and the cruiser package after 13-14 further, 62-72 simulated minutes from the start - and the cruiser clears the Pirate Base twice. Fixed earlier encounters become materially easier: the best frigate fit never clears Armored Hold over ten seeds, the destroyer always does; the railgun cruiser clears the Pirate Base in 78 s against 361 s for the blaster destroyer, and every time where the artillery destroyer clears it 7 times in 10. Larger hulls keep their disadvantages: the railgun cruiser clears Knife Fight 4 times in 10 and Range Check once, and cruiser rounds and repairs cost several times the frigate's and destroyer's; each step up costs more to field and to lose.

requirements.title: Retreat, purchased-hull loss, stored-ship reuse and recovery stay viable
requirements.extent: Phase 1: loss of a purchased hull with a usable, an unusable or no stored ship, shipless purchases and starter recovery. Phase 6, career level: a destroyer bought bare too early and lost leaves the stored frigate active without a grant, one autocannon rebuilds it and the easy site pays the way back; a lost cruiser leaves the stored destroyer active and profitable. Selective kills followed by retreat earn less per minute than clearing the site, and no insurance choice makes a deliberate loss pay.

requirements.title: Deterministic v0.2 resume; old, future and incompatible saves fail safely
requirements.extent: Phases 0-1: multi-ship resume, v0.1/future/undeclared-content rejection without alteration, explicit reset and replace confirmation. Phase 3: format 12 with guided projectiles in flight, the format 11 to 12 migration, and mid-flight resume reproducing the uninterrupted result. Phase 4: format 13 with speed effects and module targets, the format 12 to 13 migration, and mid-effect, mid-cycle resume reproducing the uninterrupted result. Phase 5: a campaign saved under earlier 0.2.0 content learns the ladder's new sites on load, and selective kills, retreat, save and return pay each bounty once and never reroll a wreck. Phase 7: the authored ladder fights reopened every 3.7 simulated seconds through the save envelope (Bombardment Line with guided volleys in flight on both sides, Range Check under both sides' webs, the Command Group with a mixed railgun, launcher and blaster cruiser) match the uninterrupted fight at every reopen, with reserved rounds, kills and each bounty paid once; a damaged, insured stored ship and an open draft for it resume and still commit to that ship alone; in the browser a v0.1 save is explained, left untouched and replaced only on confirmation; a twenty-sortie session keeps its saves bounded.

requirements.title: Browser loop from purchase to harder site and reopen
requirements.extent: Phases 3 and 5, Chromium: the guided slice (buy and fit a launcher, guided volleys, reopen in flight) and the progression loop (buy a destroyer, switch, fit blasters and a web, choose a site by band and briefing, web and destroy the cutter, loot, repair and resupply, warp to an advanced site, close and reopen there), by mouse and keyboard. Phase 7: both flows and the whole browser suite in Firefox as well; the accessibility pass over the enlarged surfaces in Chromium and Firefox - a hangar of three ships and its comparison, switching ship from the keyboard, the market's purpose, size and compatibility filters, twelve destinations in bands with a filter and keyboard choice, a fight under guided fire with reduced motion and a fight under a web - each audited, operable without a pointer and stated in words; offline operation as before.

requirements.title: Human playtest confirms fit decisions and hull progression
requirements.extent: Phase 6 prepared the human playtest route (docs/agent-comm/release/v02-playtest-route.md): start unaided, contrasting fits, an explainable failure, both hull upgrades, revisiting an earlier threat, recovering from a loss and the advanced band, with questions mapped to the acceptance criteria. Pending: the human review. Automated evidence cannot substitute for it.

candidate.$comment: The release candidate (MVP Implementation Plan phase 21; v0.2 Implementation Plan phase 7). Written by npm run release:record from a green release gate; do not edit by hand. A change to the sources or the bundle makes it stale until the gate has passed again.
